Riding light (first light to last light, Vancouver): Sat, Nov 7 7:36am to 6:16pm; Sun, Nov 8 7:37am to 6:14pm; Mon, Nov 9 7:39am to 6:13pm. Hours outside that are dark and not listed; never suggest riding then.

Guillermo's own take for Sat, Nov 7 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Outflow day in Howe Sound. Environment Canada has a gale warning, northerly 25 to 35 this morning. At 5am Pam Rocks read only N 8 gusting 15, so it's behind the page for now, but the English Bay buoy already has NNE 15 and Pemberton is 2 hPa above Vancouver.

My pick is Porteau from 9am to 1pm, NNE 26 to 28 on the page, with swell up to about 3.5ft around midday. The tide drops to 9.8ft near 11am, then floods. Go if Pam Rocks reads 22+ from the north by 9am.

Late afternoon, Howe Sound may flip to a southerly inflow.

Rider weed reports (floating weed or eelgrass, last 3 days; mention them when suggesting these spots): Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal Causeway: lots of weed (Fri, Nov 6 12:00).

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 04:00 PM PCT 07 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Tonight and Sunday. Gale warning in effect. Wind northerly outflow 25 to 35 knots becoming southerly inflow 30 to 40 early this evening with gusts to 50 then diminishing to southerly inflow 20 to 30 Sunday morning. Wind diminishing to southerly inflow 10 to 20 Sunday afternoon then becoming northerly outflow 10 to 15 Sunday evening.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 04:00 PM PCT 07 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Tonight and Sunday. Gale warning in effect. Wind southeast 20 to 30 knots becoming southeast 25 to 35 early this evening except southeast 35 to 45 south of Tsawwassen. Wind becoming south 25 to 35 late this evening with gusts to 45 and becoming south 20 to 30 Sunday morning. Wind diminishing to southwest 10 to 20 Sunday afternoon then becoming east 5 to 15 Sunday evening.
